node.label: Urbanisation & local bodies
node.summary: Census definitions of urban areas, the 74th Amendment, municipal finance and planning.

facts.text: The **16th Finance Commission** raised urban local bodies' share of local grants to **45%** and created a **₹10,000-crore 'urbanisation premium'**; the **Economic Survey 2026** said India was **63%** urban in functional terms (satellite data, 2015). India's municipal revenue is only about **1% of GDP**.
facts.plain: The 16th Finance Commission raised urban local bodies' share of local grants to 45% and created a ₹10,000-crore 'urbanisation premium'; the Economic Survey 2026 said India was 63% urban in functional terms (satellite data, 2015). India's municipal revenue is only about 1% of GDP.

facts.text: The **74th Amendment (1992)** created urban local bodies; the **Twelfth Schedule** lists **18** municipal functions. **Art. 243Q** lets States notify urban areas; **243ZD** (District Planning Committee) and **243ZE** (Metropolitan Planning Committee).
facts.plain: The 74th Amendment (1992) created urban local bodies; the Twelfth Schedule lists 18 municipal functions. Art. 243Q lets States notify urban areas; 243ZD (District Planning Committee) and 243ZE (Metropolitan Planning Committee).

facts.text: Census towns must meet three criteria: population at least **5,000**, density at least **400 per sq km**, and at least **75%** of male workers in non-farm work. India had **377 million** urban residents in **2011**; the UN puts the urban share at about 44% today.
